Project file 04 / founder work

TapeItOut —
make hardware easier to try.

A semiconductor tooling effort spanning open-source ASIC flows and a longer-term creative environment for hardware.

Yosys · LibreLane · OpenROAD · OpenSTABuilding
01 / The immediate work
02 / Product direction
03 / The line between them

The immediate work

My current founder work is flow automation around open-source ASIC tools: synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing and timing analysis, with regression automation and QoR reporting.

Current principle: every run should leave a useful record—what passed, what failed, what is inconclusive, and which artifacts support the claim.

The longer product direction

TapeItOut’s broader vision is a free-forever creative environment for hardware: start visually, simulate, revise, share and gradually move toward HDL, FPGA and ASIC work. The vision is intentionally bigger than the first implementation.

What I am not claiming

The full creative platform is not presented here as a released product. Current work is focused on flow automation and proving that the core workflow can be useful before expanding it.

What comes next

Keep the execution path reproducible, make run evidence understandable, and validate the workflow with real learners and designers before building out the larger environment.
